placements.title: Strategic decisions and knowledge governance
placements.frame: What strategic directives shape what the organization retains, decides, or erases from its record?
placements.why: Both directives are strategic acts of knowledge governance — the account holder commands what institutional knowledge persists and what is discarded. No existing strata category covers this organizational domain; mint Strategy as the top-level category these knowledge-governance directives belong under.

placements.title: Commanding organizational forgetting
placements.frame: How does directing the erasure or forgetting of institutional knowledge perform governance over what the record retains?
placements.why: Both segments are imperative directives commanding the recipient to alter their knowledge state — one to forget a named decision, the other to remove all knowledge of a named migration. They share the same thematic core: directed knowledge erasure as a governance act over the organizational record. This names a subject future envelopes may feed (what gets forgotten, by whose authority, and with what scope). No existing leaf holds this theme; the graph is empty.
